newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SWIMMING-PANKRATOV AMONG RUSSIANS BATTLING FLU EPIDEMIC.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-PANKRATOV AMONG RUSSIANS BATTLING FLU EPIDEMIC.

text.p: Olympic champion Denis Pankratov and some of his Russian team mates are battling a flu epidemic at a training camp near Moscow as they prepare for a World Cup event in less than a fortnight.

"We've had a lot of swimmers who have been called up to the training camp at Ramenskoye who have been affected to varying degrees by flu," head coach Viktor Avdiyenko told Reuters at the start of his first full season in charge of the Russian team.

Pankratov, double Olympic butterfly champion and world record-holder, had had a touch of flu which had prompted him to cut back his training schedule. But, Avdiyenko said, he would be ready for a World Cup short-course meeting in Gelsenkirchen, Germany, on February 1 and 2, providing he had no further illness.
Pankratov has fully recovered after hurting his leg when the team bus was involved in an accident in Moscow last autumn.

Double Olympic freestyle champion Alexander Popov will not travel to Germany. He has returned to train in Australia after recovering in Moscow from a stab wound in the stomach he sustained in a dispute with a roadside melon-seller last August.
Barring flu and accidents, world 200 metres backstroke champion Vladimir Selkov and European 200 metres breaststroke champion Andrei Korneyev will travel to Gelsenkirchen next week, Avdiyenko said.
But he added that the Russians did not expect to exert themselves too greatly this early in the season.

"The team isn't setting itself a great task," he said. "This is only the beginning of the season for us and we are looking forward to the major events of the year like the European championships this summer."

Nonetheless, the Russians have already made a mark on the current eight-venue World Cup series, with Nina Zhivanevskaya setting a European short-course record in the women's 100 metres backstroke at the Beijing meeting earlier this month.

Avdiyenko was appointed head coach in November after a string of successes at the Volgograd club in central Russia. He devised the revolutionary underwater technique which earned Pankratov the nickname "human submarine" and also coached Yevgeny Sadovy to triple success at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics.
